description: Configuration vectors: create and update_limits field domains, the time to live on queued payouts, approvals required, atomic allowlist changes at MAX_BATCH entries, the attestation policy, derived values and views.

vectors.description: update_limits replaces all six fields at once and emits them; the new cap and time to live apply to the next request.
Each field outside its domain, a cap above the budget, and an expiry at or before now are CONFIG_INVALID and change no limit.
The edges of every domain are accepted: TTL 3600 and 2592000, a cap equal to the budget, threshold 0, expiry one second ahead and I128_MAX.
A negative budget, cap, daily cap or threshold is CONFIG_INVALID.
A budget, daily cap or threshold one above I128_MAX is CONFIG_INVALID.
With 100 spent, 600 pending and 100 committed a budget of 799 is BUDGET_BELOW_RESERVED, a domain error is reported first, and 800 is accepted.
With no approvers a threshold at or below the cap is CONFIG_INVALID, whichever field moved; above the cap it is accepted.
update_limits from an agent is refused, and after revoke even the principal's is MANDATE_REVOKED.
A shorter time to live applies to the next request only; the payout queued before keeps its expiry, and both execute in time.
A new time to live neither shortens nor lengthens a queued payout: the new short one lapses first, and a later long one does not revive the old.
With three approvers, 0 and 4 are CONFIG_INVALID while 3 and then 1 are accepted.
With no approvers only 0 is accepted.
An approver cannot be removed below approvals_required, nor the last one while the threshold is within the cap; each works once fixed.
allow_recipients and disallow_recipients with MAX_BATCH entries apply every entry and emit one event each, in order.
allow_recipients and disallow_recipients with 0 or MAX_BATCH + 1 entries are BATCH_INVALID and change nothing.
One bad entry refuses the whole allow or disallow call, so none of its good entries are applied.
An ATTESTED mandate keeps its mode: allow and disallow are WRONG_RECIPIENT_MODE, checked before the entry count.
set_attestation_policy replaces the attester and the country policy and raises policy_epoch by one each time.
In BOTH mode the attestation policy can be changed too, with a raw 32-byte key, and the allowlist stays.
A key of 0, 31 or 33 bytes, or of 32 zero bytes, is CONFIG_INVALID and an agent's call is refused; the policy and epoch stay.
An ALLOWLIST mandate keeps its mode: set_attestation_policy is WRONG_RECIPIENT_MODE and no epoch moves.
create by the principal at the edges of every domain succeeds, emitting the factory's event and the mandate's.
An ATTESTED mandate with an attester key, threshold 0 and the longest time to live is created.
Each configuration with a field outside its domain is CONFIG_INVALID and leaves no mandate; the same salt then works.
The attester must be set exactly when the mode needs it and be 32 non-zero bytes; each other case is CONFIG_INVALID.
A configuration that breaks several rules gets the error of the first failing check in the create order.
create from anyone but the configured principal is refused and creates nothing; the principal's own call then succeeds.
free is the balance less pending and committed while active, and the whole balance once expired or revoked.
With 600 committed of 1000, free is 400: a request or a withdrawal of 401 is refused and a withdrawal of 400 is accepted.
version, payout, daily_used and is_allowed answer for a record, a tombstone, an unknown ID and a destination pair.
Views show that refused calls wrote nothing: no record for a refused request, and a removed destination reads false.
After limits and approval changes the mandate still settles in its asset and pays the fee to the factory's fee address.
